topic: Harappan Town Planning and Great Bath
questionText: The 'Great Bath' discovered at Mohenjo-daro was a large rectangular tank situated in a courtyard. A key architectural and waterproofing feature of the Great Bath was:

options.text: Constructing the entire tank out of imported white Carrara marble
Connecting the tank directly to the Arabian Sea via an underwater aqueduct
Decorating the walls with royal dynastic relief inscriptions
Lining the brick edges with gypsum mortar and using bitumen to make the tank watertight

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Bricks, Beads and Bones - Harappan Town Planning and Great Bath):
The Great Bath on the Citadel of Mohenjo-daro had steps leading down on north and south sides. It was made watertight by setting bricks on edge and using a mortar of gypsum, with rooms on three sides and a well in one room.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText: The vast majority of the rock edicts and pillar inscriptions of Mauryan Emperor Ashoka were written in which script and language?

questionText: According to the Brahmanical texts (Dharmashastras) on Gotra rules formulated around 1000 BCE onwards:

options.text: Women retained their father's gotra throughout life in all royal dynasties
Endogamous marriage within the same gotra was compulsory across all varnas
Women were expected to adopt their husband's gotra upon marriage, and members of the same gotra could not marry
Gotra was determined strictly matrilineally through the mother's lineage

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Kinship, Caste and Class - Dharmashastras and Gotra Rules):
Two main Gotra rules: (1) Women were expected to give up their father's gotra and adopt that of their husband upon marriage, and (2) Members of the same gotra could not marry (exogamy). (Note: Satavahanas were an exception where queens retained father gotras).

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: The preservation of the Great Stupa at Sanchi from being dismantled and shipped to European museums was largely due to:

topic: Ibn Battuta's Observations on Indian Postal System
questionText: In his travelogue 'Rihla', the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta marveled at the speed and efficiency of the Delhi Sultanate postal system, describing the horse post (uluq) and the foot post known as:

options.text: Dawa (stations established every one-third of a mile with swift runners)

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Through the Eyes of Travellers - Ibn Battuta's Observations on Indian Postal System):
Ibn Battuta observed two kinds of postal systems: the horse post, called 'uluq' (stations every four miles), and the foot post, called 'dawa' (three stations per mile with runners holding copper-belled batons), which conveyed news faster than the horse post.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: The poetic verses and teachings of the 15th-century mystic poet Kabir, compiled in the Kabir Bijak and Guru Granth Sahib, are characterized by:

options.text: Rigid defense of the four-fold varna system and animal sacrifices
Rejection of external ritualism, caste hierarchies, and idol worship, describing the ultimate reality as Nirguna (formless)
Advocacy of temple construction and royal patron worship exclusively
Insistence on Vedic Sanskrit as the sole medium for spiritual salvation

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Bhakti-Sufi Traditions - Kabir's Synthesizing Spiritual Philosophy):
Kabir's poetry utilized everyday vernacular dialects to reject polytheism, temple/mosque rituals, and caste discriminations, invoking the Divine through various names (Rama, Rahim, Allah, Hari) as a formless, universal spiritual presence (Nirguna Bhakti).

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: In the royal centre of the Vijayanagara Empire, the monumental platform known as the 'Mahanavami Dibba' was the focal point for:

A private crematorium reserved for Vijayanagara queens

questionText: The 'Ain-i-Akbari', compiled by Abu'l Fazl as part of the monumental 'Akbarnama', serves as an extraordinary administrative record detailing:

options.text: A fictional romantic epic narrating Persian folk legends
The administration, army, revenue regulations (dahsala), imperial household, and cultural geography of Akbar's empire
A legal penal code modeled strictly on ancient Roman law
A collection of diplomatic correspondence between Akbar and the Ottoman Sultan

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:

questionText: The Permanent Settlement introduced in Bengal by Governor-General Lord Cornwallis in 1793 established that:

options.text: Peasants were granted absolute freehold ownership rights over farmland
Land revenue was reassessed and doubled every ten years based on crop output
The revenue demand payable by Zamindars to the East India Company was fixed permanently in perpetuity
The East India Company collected revenue directly from individual village ryots

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Colonialism and the Countryside - Permanent Settlement of Bengal 1793):
Under Cornwallis's Permanent Settlement of 1793, the revenue payable by zamindars was fixed permanently in perpetuity. If a zamindar failed to pay the revenue on time by sunset of the specified date (Sunset Law), their estate was auctioned off.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: Mahatma Gandhi commenced the historic Salt Satyagraha March on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to protest against:

options.text: The forced recruitment of Indian youth into the British colonial army
The state monopoly on the manufacture and sale of salt, which imposed an unjust tax on a basic human necessity
The partition of Bengal along communal boundaries
The introduction of English medium education in government schools

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Salt March and Civil Disobedience 1930):
Salt was chosen because it was consumed by every Indian rich or poor, and the British state monopoly and salt tax symbolized the most inhuman and pervasive form of colonial economic exploitation. The 240-mile march culminated in breaking the salt law on 6 April 1930.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.
